scope: Inspected external source leads; original code is not redistributed in this collection. These are not accepted native endpoints.

leads.what_it_proves: A real Picard/fixed-point local constructor for measurable, real-symmetric solenoidal Fourier data with finite inhomogeneous H^m square bounded by R, m >= 3. Lifespan depends on m and R.
leads.dependency_trace: The proof calls exists_varConst_fixedPoint in RegLocalAuxFix.lean, whose body obtains proved varConstMap_bound/contract estimates and constructs a limit of iterates; no local-solution witness is a theorem parameter.
leads.what_remains: The target is arbitrary physical H1 data with an H1-controlled lifespan. This constructor is H^m, m >= 3, with normalized viscosity 1 and its own Fourier carriers. Strong R3 H1 admission, L2_t H2 estimates, arbitrary-nu scaling, and native adaptation remain.
leads.copy_boundary: No licensing grant was found in the acquired snapshot; no full module or long source cutout is included. README also states the patched package was not rebuilt.

leads.what_it_proves: Constructs a finite-horizon H3 Fourier solution from initial H3 data and one uniform homogeneous-H1 bound for every shorter symbol flow from that datum.
leads.dependency_trace: The proof uses hsNormSq_apriori, the actual H3 local constructor, and finite concatenation. The norm-bound hypothesis is explicit and is not proved by this theorem.
leads.what_remains: This is useful continuation architecture, but its universal bound on shorter flows must be derived. It is not a theorem of arbitrary H1 local existence or the literal A4 competitor bound.
leads.copy_boundary: No licensing grant was found in the acquired snapshot; no full module or long source cutout is included. README also states the patched package was not rebuilt.

leads.what_it_proves: Recovers smooth physical velocity and pressure on the closed slab from all-order IsHsCurve regularity, the actual Duhamel symbol equation and solenoidal/reality conditions.
leads.dependency_trace: The proof invokes smooth_physField_curve, smooth_pressure_curve, Fourier derivative/nonlinear/pressure identities and derives actual momentum and divergence.
leads.what_remains: All Sobolev orders are supplied. Their propagation from Schwartz data and the P10 physical H1 construction must be linked. IsSolutionOn is viscosity-normalized; the arbitrary-nu adapter is still required.
leads.copy_boundary: No licensing grant was found in the acquired snapshot; no full module or long source cutout is included. README also states the patched package was not rebuilt.

leads.what_it_proves: Compares two actual smooth viscosity-1 solutions on a closed R3 slab, with a finite uniform slab L2-energy bound for each and a common velocity-and-gradient supremum bound only for the reference, assuming the same initial velocity.
leads.dependency_trace: The proof uses localized difference energy, actual pressure replacement and an error vanishing as the spatial cutoff radius tends to infinity; it does not assume H3 for the competitor.
leads.what_remains: GradientBoundedOn bounds both reference velocity and its derivative. Uniqueness on each R < Tmax does not by itself produce a uniform H1/enstrophy bound as R approaches a finite Tmax for a literal smooth finite-energy competitor. Thus the closed-slab admission/continuation part of A4 remains open in the target.

leads.what_it_proves: Proves the implication from LocalGain, MildRestrict and DerivSobolev to all-order homogeneous Sobolev regularity on slabs separated from the initial time for an already supplied mild X trajectory.
leads.dependency_trace: The body bootstraps derivative bounds and interpolation. RegularStatements.lean spells out that IsMildX is an input; PicardConverges also assumes a mild trajectory. These are useful smoothing components, not that trajectory's existence.
leads.what_remains: The three analytic premises need their proved instances and native transport; the closed initial boundary for Schwartz data, physical H1 carrier and viscosity scaling remain. Directory name CertTorus does not make this a spatially periodic lemma; its X is a whole-space Fourier carrier.
